initialize.instructions: IDA Pro reverse engineering of compiled binaries (ELF, PE, Mach-O, firmware): decompile to pseudocode, disassemble (disasm), xrefs, symbols, strings, imports, types. Use instead of objdump, readelf, nm or strings when you need decompilation or cross-references. open_database(path) only opens a path on this MCP server. Remote samples must be uploaded first: upload_begin, upload_chunk in a loop, upload_finish, then open_database with the returned server path.

tools.name: open_database
tools.description:
Open (load) a binary executable, shared library, firmware image, or an
existing .i64/.idb IDA database in IDA Pro for reverse engineering. Runs IDA
auto-analysis (functions, disassembly, cross references, strings) in a headless
idalib worker, or attaches to the file already open in the IDA GUI. Call this
first, then use execute_python to decompile, disassemble and query the binary.
load_options apply only when a new headless worker is spawned; they do not
change an already-open IDA GUI database or a reused worker.

path.description: Path to a local executable or IDB. A GUI instance is used when available.

set_current.description: Whether this database should become the default target for execute_python().

processor.description: IDA processor module, such as metapc.

file_type.description: IDA input file type, such as binary.

image_base.description: Image base byte address; must be 16-byte aligned.

load_options.description: IDA import options for a newly spawned worker, such as loading a raw blob.

tools.title: Open binary in IDA

recovery.description: Crash recovery performed while opening: none, repaired, or restored.

tools.name: execute_python
tools.description:
Run Python (IDAPython and the ida-domain API) against the binary open in IDA:
decompile a function to Hex-Rays pseudocode, disassemble (disasm) instructions,
enumerate functions, strings, imports, exports, symbols, segments and sections,
find cross references (xrefs to/from an address, callers, callees, call graph),
get the function at an address, inspect or apply types and structs, rename
functions and variables, add comments, and patch bytes. Returns the result plus
stdout/stderr. Look up API names with reference first.

code.description: Python code that runs against an already-open database. Call reference(query) first; do not guess the API shape. `db` is the current ida-domain Database, and `ida_domain` is also imported globally. Imports, variables, and definitions persist for this agent's database lease. A single or trailing expression is returned. For function-style code, define run(db), execute(db), or main(db); it is invoked automatically when there is no trailing expression.

instance_id.description: Optional database instance id. If omitted, use the current target.

timeout.description: Python execution timeout in seconds. This does not include the separate initial autoanalysis wait.

tools.title: Run IDA Python analysis

tools.name: reference
tools.description:
Look up the IDA Pro ida-domain Python API by task or name, e.g.
"decompile function", "xrefs to address", "list strings",
"rename local variable", "struct type". Returns API signatures and usage
examples for IDA analysis via execute_python.

query.description: Class, method, or reverse-engineering concept to look up in the IDA reference.

tools.title: Search IDA API reference

tools.name: list_databases
tools.description:
Show the IDA databases (analyzed binaries, .i64/.idb) currently open in the
IDA GUI or in headless idalib workers, with their instance ids.
tools.title: Show open IDA databases

status.description: Action state: available, attached, current, or unavailable.

tools.name: save_database
tools.description:
Save the IDA database (.i64) to disk so renames, comments, types and patches
made during reverse engineering persist.

instance_id.description: Optional database instance id. If omitted, save the current target.

tools.title: Save IDA database

tools.name: close_database
tools.description:
Release this session's lease on an IDA database (.i64/.idb) without
disrupting other clients. If this is the final lease on a managed idalib worker,
orphaned IDA Python execution is cancelled and this call waits for the IDB to
shut down. Databases open in the IDA GUI stay open.

instance_id.description: Optional database instance id. If omitted, release the current target.

tools.title: Release IDA database

tools.name: upload_begin
tools.description:
Start a chunked upload into the server inbox.

Recommended flow for a remote agent: upload_begin -> upload_chunk in a loop
-> upload_finish -> open_database(path). This tool does not call
open_database. The sample must land on this server; a path on the agent
disk cannot be opened here.

filename.description: Original sample filename. Only the basename is kept; empty names become sample.bin.

size.description: Total size of the sample in bytes.

sha256.description: Optional SHA-256 hex digest checked when upload_finish is called.

tools.title: Begin sample upload

tools.name: upload_chunk
tools.description:
Write one chunk of an in-progress inbox upload.

Recommended flow: upload_begin -> upload_chunk in a loop -> upload_finish ->
open_database(path). This tool does not call open_database. The same offset
may be retried; unfinished uploads survive server restart and can continue
with the same upload_id.

offset.description: Byte offset to write. Retrying the same range overwrites it.

data_base64.description: Base64-encoded chunk. Decoded size must not exceed 1 MiB.

tools.title: Upload sample chunk

tools.name: upload_finish
tools.description:
Complete an inbox upload and return a server-local path.

Recommended flow: upload_begin -> upload_chunk in a loop -> upload_finish ->
open_database(path). This tool does not call open_database. Pass the returned
absolute path to open_database unchanged.

sha256.description: Optional SHA-256 hex digest. Overrides the digest from upload_begin when set.

tools.title: Finish sample upload

tools.name: list_uploads
tools.description:
List pending and completed samples in the server inbox.

Recommended flow: upload_begin -> upload_chunk in a loop -> upload_finish ->
open_database(path). This tool does not call open_database.
tools.title: List inbox uploads

tools.name: delete_upload
tools.description:
Delete one inbox upload. Paths outside the inbox are rejected.

Recommended flow: upload_begin -> upload_chunk in a loop -> upload_finish ->
open_database(path). This tool does not call open_database. If the sample is
held by a database lease, close_database first.
tools.title: Delete inbox upload
